correctness.rationale: The geometric-fixed orbit model follows from barycentric coordinate equality under an involution. Orbit compatibility is equivalent to strict nesting plus at most one central diagonal. This gives a bijection with all nonempty subsets of [n], four universal isolated orbit vertices, and one further connected component. The actual embedded independent program enumerates every simplex for n=3..8 and computes all integer boundary Smith forms; n=8 has face counts (36,126,84,9), boundary ranks (31,67,9), every nonzero Smith invariant equal to 1, hence reduced H0=Z4, H1=Z28, H2=Z8, and others zero. For n=3..7 H2=0; n<=2 has dimension<2. The universal f-vector and Euler formula are proved symbolically.

value.rationale: The coordinate swap is the distinguished nontrivial symmetry of the square member of a recent naturally studied graph-poset family. Its actual fixed space cannot be recovered from ordinary Betti numbers or an unspecified nonequivariant wedge decomposition. The full orbit-combinatorial f-vector and five-component theorem hold uniformly, and the first appearance of integral H2 at n=8 is a motivated sharp finite cutoff, with eight free generators and no torsion. This distinguishes new higher-dimensional geometric fixed topology despite the stable number of connected components, without asserting an unproved infinite homology pattern.
